Eames inside your room

Original chair and ottoman inside the server-selected room (verified on Render). No added studio walls or ceiling panel. External daylight is supplied because the room has no authored lights.

Experimental adaptive sampling: known lighting artifacts remain. Six bounces. Optional rough-surface denoising changes presentation only. Not real-time or quality-qualified.

Placement moves the Eames chair and ottoman together; the comparison camera target stays fixed. Centre reference exchanges the sofa and spacesuit floor positions without changing their rotation; it has no effect in Eames-only mode. The first additional seating model is uniformly scaled to 1.5 m wide, preserving its proportions; the standing model keeps its source scale. Authored materials are unchanged unless the explicit seat-wood varnish variant is enabled. Changes apply on Render; wall collisions are not checked. FOV defaults to 52° (previously 62°); this remains a single-camera, not stereo, view.

Clearcoat is a separate transparent surface finish, not a tint or a second mesh. The optional varnish variant coats only verified seat wood; strength and roughness are adjustable. It requires the layered-clearcoat switch. Original model files are never rewritten. Both switches reset off. These controls apply to Render room only, not the cloth diagnostic or splitting benchmark.

Additional assets are loaded only from the local server and verified on Render.

Room lighting is selectable and intensity is adjustable. Cool evening is an artistic colour study, not a solar-position simulation. Models, light direction and exposure are unchanged. Reset restores original daylight. Lighting applies to Render room and the splitting comparison; the separate white-light diagnostic below keeps its own illumination.

The cloth diagnostic uses the selected camera and SPP ceiling, uniform stable camera samples and the selected sheen model. It compares normal maps on/off and pixel-centre/multi-sample camera rays under one unoccluded white light. It omits shadows, indirect bounces, splitting and denoising. Not a full render or performance benchmark; no authored texture changes.

Splitting requires the stable sampler. It adds secondary rays, not camera SPP. No split after the selected depth.

Close-up moves the camera, not the model or its texture scale. Uniform sampling removes radial quality bands. Material inspection requires guided denoising: it displays the same frame's first-sample base colour and mapped world normals, not another renderer. Colour includes the authored tint; magenta normals mean unavailable/protected. These single-sample guides are not antialiased or photographic output.

Splitting benchmark uses room-view framing, radial budgets at the default ceiling, denoising off and the stable sampler for every variant. Close-up and material-inspection controls do not apply. One warmup, three rotated timing rounds, then diagnostic images. Keep this tab visible; it may take several minutes.

Ready. Render to view the Eames inside the room.
